differences_from_cancho_web_examples_use: the application half only: cancho-web's example has its own server loop; here the loop is the shared skeleton and the example's `handle` becomes app_handle over `&!a App`
state is fixed (Box slices written in place, at most 200 users) instead of a growing buffer and Vec: a borrowed App cannot swap in a grown collection
no offset parameter, no email/role/tags fields, no /health, no filler routes; a body of exactly name (1-40 code points) and age (0-150)
two pure units (json_type_ok, has_room); the rest is the integration unit
pitfalls: web.respond_problem refers to #/components/responses/Problem, which the generated document contains only if a component named `Problem` is declared; without it the served OpenAPI document has a dangling $ref and nothing complains (found by writing the attack; the attack checks that every $ref resolves)
schema slots are numbered by add_field calls across the whole schema in call order: the fields of the request body must be added first, or the slot constants shift
web.default_int needs the Schema borrowed (`borrow s as &sr in { ... }`); without a declared default an absent limit reads as 0 and the page is empty
operation ids are the order of declaration (1, 2, ...); web.internal also takes an id; the handler compares dispatch's answer with them
a tape for a body is a box_slice, not a region (a region is one 64 KiB chunk)
schema.problem and web.dispatch write application/problem+json, but the 405 body of dispatch is {"error":"method not allowed"} with an Allow header (application/json); the brief says only 405 + Allow
the library accepts \u0000 in a name unless schema.forbid_nul is called; the brief does not say, the attack does not test it
limit=007 and limit=%31 are accepted by dispatch (leading zeros, percent-decoding); not in the brief, not tested
